answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each identity to post a refundable stake bonded to a unique verifiable credential, like a quartz seal that cannot be copied cheaply. One honest agent pays once, while an attacker spawning thousands of sparrow identities must lock capital and pay verification fees for every one, so the cost scales linearly with the attack. Honest work slowly earns the stake back, but detected fraud forfeits it, turning a zephyr of cheap fakes into an expensive, losing strategy.
